attractions.name: Burj Khalifa
attractions.shortIntro: The world’s tallest architectural icon rising 828 meters above Downtown Dubai.
attractions.description: Soaring over Downtown Dubai, Burj Khalifa anchors the city skyline with observation decks on Levels 124, 125, and 148, surrounded by the choreographed Dubai Fountain and Burj Park promenade.
attractions.location: Downtown Dubai, Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Blvd
facts: Stands 828 meters (2,717 feet) tall with more than 160 stories.
High-speed elevators ascend to Level 124 in roughly one minute.
Its Y-shaped floor plan draws inspiration from the desert spider lily (Hymenocallis).

attractions.name: Dubai Mall
attractions.shortIntro: A premier shopping, dining, and entertainment destination beside Burj Khalifa.
attractions.description: Located at the foot of Burj Khalifa, Dubai Mall pairs over 1,200 retail stores with indoor attractions including the Dubai Aquarium & Underwater Zoo, Dubai Ice Rink, and waterfront dining terraces.
facts: Houses a 10-million-liter aquarium tank visible directly from the main atrium.
Connects directly to the Burj Khalifa observation deck entrance and Dubai Fountain boardwalk.

attractions.name: Museum of the Future
attractions.shortIntro: A torus-shaped architectural landmark dedicated to science, space, and future design.
attractions.description: Framed in stainless steel engraved with Arabic calligraphy along Sheikh Zayed Road, the Museum of the Future invites visitors through interactive exhibitions exploring space habitats, climate ecosystems, and human wellbeing.
attractions.location: Sheikh Zayed Road, Trade Centre 2, Dubai
facts: Engineered without internal structural columns across its 77-meter-tall torus shell.
Its facade features 1,024 stainless-steel panels engraved with inspirational poetry.

attractions.name: Burj Al Arab
attractions.shortIntro: Dubai’s sail-shaped coastal silhouette perched on its own man-made island.
attractions.description: Rising 321 meters off Jumeirah Beach, Burj Al Arab is celebrated worldwide for its billowing dhow-sail architecture, connecting to the mainland by a sweeping private causeway.
attractions.location: Umm Suqeim 3, Jumeirah Beach Road, Dubai
facts: Built on a dedicated artificial island 280 meters offshore from Jumeirah Beach.
Famous sunset viewpoints are located along Sunset Beach and Souk Madinat Jumeirah.

attractions.name: Palm Jumeirah
attractions.shortIntro: An engineered palm-tree island crowned with crescent resorts and waterfront dining.
attractions.description: Extending into the Arabian Gulf, Palm Jumeirah features a central trunk lined with beach clubs and residences, 16 residential fronds, and an 11-kilometer outer crescent connected by boardwalks and monorail.
facts: Constructed entirely from natural sand and rock without steel or concrete foundations.
The View at The Palm offers a 360-degree vantage point 240 meters above the island.

attractions.name: Atlantis The Palm
attractions.shortIntro: The iconic arch-crowned coastal resort anchoring the apex of Palm Jumeirah.
attractions.description: Positioned at the tip of the Palm Jumeirah crescent, Atlantis The Palm is renowned for its grand Arabian-inspired central archway, Aquaventure Waterpark, and Lost Chambers marine habitats.
facts: The Palm Monorail terminates directly at Atlantis Aquaventure station.
Its crescent boardwalk provides sweeping views of the Dubai Marina skyline.

attractions.name: Dubai Frame
attractions.shortIntro: A 150-meter golden architectural frame bridging Old and New Dubai.
attractions.description: Set inside Zabeel Park, the Dubai Frame literally frames views of historic Deira and Karama to the north and Sheikh Zayed Road’s skyscrapers to the south from its sky-bridge glass walkway.
attractions.location: Zabeel Park Jogging Track, Za’abeel, Dubai
facts: Comprises two 150-meter vertical towers joined by a 93-meter glass-floored bridge.
Exterior cladding pattern is inspired by the Expo 2020 geometric motif.

attractions.name: Dubai Marina
attractions.shortIntro: A vibrant waterfront canal district framed by yachts, cafés, and illuminated towers.
attractions.description: Carved along a three-kilometer stretch of shoreline, Dubai Marina offers an active 7-kilometer waterside promenade, yacht departures, dining terraces, and pedestrian access to JBR and Bluewaters Island.
facts: One of the world’s largest man-made marina developments.
Connected by footbridge directly to Bluewaters Island.

attractions.name: Jumeirah Beach
attractions.shortIntro: White sandy Arabian Gulf shoreline with uninterrupted views of Burj Al Arab.
attractions.description: Stretching along Dubai’s coast, Jumeirah Beach offers calm turquoise waters, scenic coastal jogging paths, and the classic open-air photography vantage looking toward Burj Al Arab.
facts: Popular during late afternoon golden hour for unobstructed coastal photography.
Features landscaped beachfront walkways and shaded coastal parks.

attractions.name: Dubai Creek
attractions.shortIntro: The historic saltwater inlet where Dubai’s maritime trading heritage began.
attractions.description: Dividing Bur Dubai and Deira, Dubai Creek remains alive with traditional wooden abra ferries, dhow cargo boats, Al Seef heritage walkways, and bustling Gold and Spice Souks.
facts: Wooden abra boats still ferry commuters and visitors across the creek daily.
Bordered by the preserved coral-stone wind towers of Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood.

attractions.name: Global Village
attractions.shortIntro: Dubai’s seasonal open-air multicultural pavilion park, street food hub, and evening festival.
attractions.description: Operating during Dubai’s cooler winter months, Global Village gathers cultural pavilions from dozens of countries alongside artisan crafts, floating markets, live stage performances, and international street cuisine.
attractions.location: Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road (E311), Dubai
facts: Seasonal attraction open primarily from October through April/May.
Best visited in the evening when pavilion facades and fireworks illuminate the park.

attractions.name: Dubai Miracle Garden
attractions.shortIntro: A sprawling seasonal botanical showcase featuring tens of millions of blooming flowers.
attractions.description: Located in Dubailand, Dubai Miracle Garden transforms desert landscape into floral arches, heart tunnels, and life-size botanical sculptures during the cooler winter season.
facts: Seasonal attraction open during cooler months (typically November to April).
Showcases floral installations maintained through drip irrigation.

cms.faqSubtitle: Browse answers grouped by Tours, Transfers, and Booking to plan your Dubai itinerary clearly.

faqs.question: What are the Desert Safari rates for per-person and private 4x4 bookings?
faqs.answer: Our sharing-basis Desert Safari is 120 AED per person, and our Private 4x4 Desert Safari for 5 to 6 guests is 800 AED total. Both include dune drives, sunset viewpoints, and Arabian desert camp hospitality.

faqs.question: Do city and private sightseeing tours offer Half-Day and Full-Day AED rates?
faqs.answer: Yes. Clear Half-Day (4 Hours, up to 250 AED) and Full-Day (8 Hours, up to 500 AED) rates are available in AED — including Half-Day Dubai Tour (250 AED), Full-Day Dubai Tour (500 AED), Dubai City Tour (250 AED Half-Day / 500 AED Full-Day), Old Dubai Heritage Tour (200 AED Half-Day / 420 AED Full-Day), and Abu Dhabi City Tour (500 AED Full-Day).

faqs.question: Who organizes the programs and leads the guided tours?
faqs.answer: All itineraries, schedules, and transfers are organized by Program Organizer Shahzaman Khokhar, while sightseeing tours and cultural walks are led in English by Tour Guides Usama and Abdul Qadir.

faqs.question: What are the Dubai Airport (DXB) arrival and departure transfer rates?
faqs.answer: Dubai Airport (DXB) arrival transfers to Old Dubai (Deira & Bur Dubai) are 120 AED, and departures from Old Dubai back to DXB are 100 AED. Both arrivals and departures for New Dubai (Dubai Marina, Palm Jumeirah, and Downtown) are 170 AED per way.

faqs.question: What do inter-hotel transfers cost between Old Dubai and New Dubai?
faqs.answer: Inter-hotel transfers between properties within Old Dubai (Deira & Bur Dubai) are 80 AED. Inter-hotel transfers from Old Dubai to New Dubai (Marina, Palm Jumeirah, or Downtown) are 150 AED.

faqs.question: Where can you pick up and drop off guests?
faqs.answer: Pickup and drop-off are available directly from any hotel or private residence in Old Dubai and New Dubai, Dubai International Airport (DXB Terminals 1, 2 & 3), as well as Port Rashid and Dubai Harbour cruise terminals.

faqs.question: How does online booking and guide confirmation work?
faqs.answer: Submitting the online booking form generates a unique reference code (TA-DXB-XXXXXX) with pending status. Your request is not finalized until Program Organizer Shahzaman Khokhar verifies availability and confirms it. You can track your request status anytime on the Book page.

faqs.question: How quickly can I coordinate pickup times or special requests on WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: You can message our WhatsApp business desk directly from any tour or transfer card, the booking confirmation page, or the floating WhatsApp button. Selected tour names, travel dates, guest counts, and pickup notes are pre-filled automatically.

faqs.question: Are attraction observation deck tickets included in sightseeing rates?
faqs.answer: Unless specified on the package, third-party tickets such as Burj Khalifa observation decks or museum passes are excluded from the guide/vehicle rate and quoted separately based on your preferred entry time.
